title: Contributing
content: Reporting Issues Search existing issues first, then open a new one with: urx --version output and your OS the command you ran expected vs actual output Development Setup You need Rust (latest stable) and Git. Fork the repo, then: git clone https://github.com/YOUR_USERNAME/urx.git cd urx cargo build cargo test urx is a binary crate: use cargo test (or cargo test --bin urx). cargo test --lib fails. Before Opening a PR Run what CI runs: cargo fmt --all -- --check cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings cargo test --all-targets --all-features also lints the tests and the optional redis-cache code, which a plain cargo clippy skips. CI uses the latest stable toolchain, so new lints can show up there first. With just, just test runs tests, clippy (code and tests), the format check and cargo doc. just fix formats and applies clippy's automatic fixes. Keep each PR to one change, add tests for new behaviour, reference related issues, and note breaking changes. Update CHANGELOG.md for significant changes. Documentation Docs live in docs/content/ (Markdown with TOML front matter) and are built with Hwaro: just docs-dependencies # install Hwaro (macOS, via Homebrew) just docs-serve # preview at http://localhost:3000 When you add or change a flag or config key, update both README.md and the pages under docs/content/guide/. The option blocks on CLI Options and in the README are copied by hand from urx --help, so diff them against the built binary's output. New config keys also go in example/config.toml and Configuration. Project Structure urx/ ├── src/ # Source code │ ├── main.rs # Entry point │ ├── app/ # Run orchestration; catalog.rs is the provider registry │ ├── cli/ # CLI argument parsing │ ├── config/ # TOML config and provider-config loading │ ├── providers/ # URL data providers │ ├── filters/ # URL filtering, presets, scope files │ ├── testers/ # Status checks, link / JS / spec extraction │ ├── runner/ # Concurrent provider runs, --max-time, Ctrl-C │ ├── tester_manager/ # Runs the testers over collected URLs │ ├── readers/ # --files readers (WARC, URLTeam, text) │ ├── cache/ # SQLite / Redis cache and the `urx cache` subcommand │ ├── output/ # Output formats and --stream │ ├── notify/ # Webhook notifications │ ├── progress/ # Progress bars │ ├── utils/ # URL transforms and helpers │ └── network/ # HTTP client, proxy, headers, rate limiting ├── tests/ # Integration tests ├── docs/ # Documentation (Hwaro site) ├── example/ # Example configurations ├── aur/ # Arch Linux package └── Dockerfile # Container image More Full guide: CONTRIBUTING.md Code of Conduct (Contributor Covenant) Contributions are licensed under the project's MIT License.

title: Installation
content: Installation Methods From Cargo Needs a Rust toolchain: cargo install urx From Homebrew brew install urx # or from the project tap brew install hahwul/urx/urx From the AUR Arch Linux, with an AUR helper: yay -S urx # or paru -S urx From Chocolatey Windows, with Chocolatey: choco install urx This installs the windows-x86_64 release binary and adds urx to PATH. From GitHub Releases Each release has prebuilt binaries, each with a .sha256 checksum: Platform Asset Linux x86_64 urx-X.Y.Z-linux-x86_64.tar.gz Linux aarch64 urx-X.Y.Z-linux-aarch64.tar.gz macOS Intel urx-X.Y.Z-macos-x86_64.tar.gz macOS Apple Silicon urx-X.Y.Z-macos-aarch64.tar.gz Windows x86_64 urx-X.Y.Z-windows-x86_64.zip Unpack it and put urx on your $PATH. From Source git clone https://github.com/hahwul/urx.git cd urx cargo build --release The binary is at target/release/urx. Optional: Redis Cache Support The Redis cache backend (--cache-type redis) is an optional Cargo feature. No packaged build (crates.io, Homebrew, AUR, Chocolatey, release binaries, Docker) includes it. Build it yourself: cargo install urx --features redis-cache # or, from a source checkout cargo build --release --features redis-cache From Docker docker pull ghcr.io/hahwul/urx:latest The image has no entrypoint, so put ./urx before the arguments: docker run --rm ghcr.io/hahwul/urx:latest ./urx example.com # piping domains in needs -i cat domains.txt | docker run --rm -i ghcr.io/hahwul/urx:latest ./urx Tags: latest, the release version (e.g. 0.11.0), and main for the development branch. Verifying Installation urx --version Shell Completions and Man Page Both are generated by the binary, so they match the installed version: # zsh (any directory on your $fpath) urx --completions zsh > ~/.zfunc/_urx # bash urx --completions bash > ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions/urx # fish urx --completions fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/urx.fish # man page urx --manpage > ~/.local/share/man/man1/urx.1 man urx powershell and elvish also work. See CLI Options. Next Steps See the Quick Start.

title: Quick Start
content: Basic Usage Single Domain urx example.com This queries the default providers (Wayback Machine, Common Crawl, OTX) plus the target's live robots.txt and sitemap.xml, and prints the URLs. Turn the last two off with --exclude-robots / --exclude-sitemap. A provider that takes an API key (vt, urlscan, zoomeye, github, bevigil) is added when its key is set, even with an explicit --providers list. See Environment Variables. Multiple Domains urx example.com example.org From Standard Input cat domains.txt | urx # or name the file directly (alias --dL) urx --domain-list domains.txt Save Output to File urx example.com -o results.txt JSON Output urx example.com -f json -o results.json Common Use Cases Security Scanning JavaScript files only: urx example.com -e js -o js-files.txt API Endpoint Discovery URLs containing any of these patterns: urx example.com --patterns api,v1,v2,graphql Exclude Common Resources Drop images and static resources with presets: urx example.com -p no-images,no-resources With HTTP Status Checking Keep only URLs that return 200: urx example.com --check-status --include-status 200 Getting Help urx --help Next Steps CLI Options Examples Configuration file

title: Caching
content: Caching & Incremental Scanning urx caches the URLs each scan collected. A repeat scan can be answered from the cache without querying providers, and an incremental scan reports only new URLs. # SQLite is the default backend; name it and its path explicitly urx example.com --cache-type sqlite --cache-path ~/.urx/cache.db # Redis (needs: cargo install urx --features redis-cache) urx example.com --cache-type redis --redis-url redis://localhost:6379 # only URLs not seen in the last scan urx example.com --incremental # cache TTL of 12 hours urx example.com --cache-ttl 43200 # no cache urx example.com --no-cache # incremental with filters urx example.com --incremental -e js,php --patterns api # every option from a config file (the example writes to results.txt, not stdout; review it first) urx -c example/config.toml example.com How It Works Caching is on by default; --no-cache turns it off. After a scan, urx stores the URLs collected for each domain in SQLite (local) or Redis (remote). Normal run: if the domain has an entry younger than --cache-ttl, urx returns the cached URLs and skips the providers for that domain. Otherwise it fetches fresh results and replaces the entry. --incremental run: urx always fetches fresh results, prints only URLs no earlier run had seen, then adds the fresh set to the baseline. The baseline only grows, so a run cut short never makes the next one re-report URLs. A cache entry belongs to one domain and one configuration. The key covers the domain (or path-scoped target), the effective provider list, and the options that change what is collected: --subs, -e / --exclude-extensions, --patterns / --exclude-patterns, --match-regex / --filter-regex, -p, --min-length / --max-length, --strict, --normalize-url, --merge-endpoint, --dedup-similar, --cc-index, --from / --to, the --archive-* filters, --archived-discovery (and a non-default --archived-discovery-limit), and --cdx-endpoint / --cdx-dialect. Change any of these and the run starts a new baseline, so an incremental scan re-reports everything once. Setting a URX_*_API_KEY variable adds that provider to the list, which also changes the key. --incremental is not part of the key: a normal run adds its URLs to the baseline an incremental run compares against (it never shrinks it), and its cache hits return that baseline. Incremental Scanning # first scan: builds the cache, outputs all URLs urx example.com --incremental -o initial.txt # later scans: only URLs new since the last run urx example.com --incremental -o new-urls.txt Output holds only URLs the previous run with the same configuration had not seen. Pair it with --notify --notify-on new to alert only when something new turns up. Every provider is still queried on each incremental run; it saves reading, not fetching. SQLite Cache (Default) The default database is $HOME/.urx/cache.db (./.urx/cache.db when HOME is not set). Use it for single-machine scanning. # default location urx example.com --incremental # custom location urx example.com --incremental --cache-path /path/to/cache.db Redis Cache Redis gives a cache shared across machines (teams, distributed or container scanning). Redis support is an optional Cargo feature. Packaged builds (crates.io, Homebrew, AUR, release binaries, Docker image) leave it out, and --cache-type redis fails with Redis cache support not compiled in. Build with cargo install urx --features redis-cache. Machines share entries only when they run with the same flags and the same keyed providers enabled. A keyed provider joins the cache key, but the key's value does not, so different keys for the same provider share entries. urx example.com --cache-type redis --redis-url redis://localhost:6379 Cache TTL The TTL sets how long an entry is served instead of a fresh fetch. Default: 86400 seconds (24 hours). It also drives cleanup. At the end of every scan, urx deletes every entry older than twice the TTL, for any domain, except entries an --incremental run wrote: those baselines are compared against with no TTL, so the sweep keeps them. urx cache prune deletes every entry older than the TTL, baselines included, and urx cache drop removes one domain's. The sweep uses the TTL of the run doing it. One run with --cache-ttl 300 deletes every non-baseline entry older than 10 minutes in that database. Give short-TTL experiments their own --cache-path. # 5 minutes, in its own cache urx example.com --cache-ttl 300 --cache-path ~/.urx/short-ttl.db # 12 hours, for daily scans urx example.com --cache-ttl 43200 # 7 days, for stable targets urx example.com --cache-ttl 604800 Disabling the Cache urx example.com --no-cache With --no-cache, --incremental has no baseline and is ignored: every URL is printed. What the Cache Does and Does Not Hold It stores the host-validated URLs the providers returned, before filters run. Filters and output views apply afterwards, on hits and misses alike. Under --no-strict it also keeps the off-host URLs, so a hit returns what the miss did; a multi-domain --no-strict run that found off-host URLs is not cached, because they cannot be attributed to one domain, and under --incremental such a run leaves them out of the baselines and the output. It stores URLs only: no provider attribution and no archive capture metadata. On a hit, --show-sources has nothing to show, JSON/CSV lack first_seen / last_seen / mime / archive_status / digest, positive --meta-* filters drop everything (--meta-exclude-* drop nothing), --archive-body has nothing to replay, and --stats stays empty. Add --no-cache when you need those. --stream and --files bypass the cache. A normal run does not cache a domain that --max-time, Ctrl-C or a provider error left incomplete, nor one that returned no URLs; the next run fetches it again. An --incremental run adds whatever it got to the baseline, even a partial set, which is safe because the baseline never shrinks. A cache backend that can't be opened (an unreachable Redis server, say) is a fatal error. There is no silent fallback. Inspecting and Maintaining the Cache urx cache inspects and maintains the cache. Every subcommand honours the same --cache-type, --cache-path, --redis-url and --cache-ttl a scan uses, so it reports what a scan would see. All five work on both backends. Command What it does urx cache stats Entries, domains, URLs, age span, size (database file for SQLite, stored bytes for Redis), expired count urx cache list [--domain PAT] Per-domain entry and URL counts, last scan time, TTL remaining urx cache prune Delete only what --cache-ttl has expired urx cache drop <DOMAIN>... Delete every entry for the given domains urx cache clear [-y|--yes] Delete everything, confirming first $ urx cache stats Cache: sqlite Location: /home/you/.urx/cache.db Size: 4.2 MiB (database file) Entries: 312 Domains: 27 URLs: 184,905 Expired: 41 (--cache-ttl 86400s = 1d 0h) Oldest: 2026-09-08T19:02:44Z (1d 20h ago) Newest: 2026-09-09T22:41:02Z (16h 12m ago) $ urx cache list --domain '*.example.com' DOMAIN ENTRIES EXPIRED URLS LAST SCAN TTL LEFT ---------------- ------- ------- --------- -------------------- -------- api.example.com 2 0 12,884 2026-09-09T22:41:02Z 7h 47m shop.example.com 1 1 3,201 2026-09-08T19:02:44Z expired # cached domains and their remaining TTL urx cache list # one program's hosts urx cache list --domain '*.example.com' # rescan one target from scratch, keep the rest urx cache drop example.com # drop only what has expired urx cache prune # delete everything without the prompt urx cache clear --yes # a shared Redis cache urx cache stats --cache-type redis --redis-url redis://cache-server:6379 Domain patterns: list --domain and drop match case-insensitively and exactly, unless the pattern contains * (any run of characters). *.example.com matches subdomains only, example.* any TLD, *example* any domain containing the text. So drop example.com does not touch notexample.com. JSON output: -f json switches every subcommand to JSON (-f jsonl prints the same document; other -f values print plain text). urx cache stats -f json | jq '.expired_entries' urx cache list -f json | jq -r '.[] | select(.ttl_remaining == null) | .domain' Other behaviour: Looking at the cache never creates one. A first-ever urx cache stats reports the location as "does not exist yet". clear asks before deleting and refuses a non-interactive stdin. Use --yes in scripts. drop names any pattern that matched nothing, so a typo doesn't look like success. On Redis, urx cache sweeps with SCAN (never the blocking KEYS) and redacts any password in --redis-url before printing it. Keys are urx:cache:<sha256> and urx:meta:<sha256>. urx manages expiry itself and sets no Redis EXPIRE. urx cache reads -c / --config and the [cache] section like a scan does, and ignores no_cache / --no-cache. --no-cache is only accepted before cache; --cache-type, --cache-path, --redis-url, --cache-ttl and -f work in either position. Combined Examples # daily monitoring: webhook fires only when something new turns up # (see --notify in CLI Options) urx example.com --incremental --silent --notify "$URX_HOOK" --notify-format slack # hand new URLs to an external notifier # (--silent would hide stdout too; --no-progress only hides the progress bar) urx target.com --incremental --no-progress | notify-tool # domain lists (keep --cache-ttl above the scan interval: entries older than 2x TTL are swept) cat domains.txt | urx --incremental --no-progress > new_urls.txt # shared Redis cache (needs a redis-cache build) urx example.com --cache-type redis --redis-url redis://shared-cache:6379 # fast re-scans: 5-minute TTL in a separate cache, since a short TTL sweeps # every older entry in the database it runs against urx test-domain.com --cache-ttl 300 --cache-path /tmp/urx-scratch.db Configuration File Caching can also be set in a config file: [cache] incremental = true cache_type = "sqlite" # or "redis" cache_path = "/home/me/.urx/cache.db" # `~` is not expanded; omit for the default # redis_url = "redis://localhost:6379" cache_ttl = 86400 no_cache = false

title: CLI Options
content: Command Line Options Output of urx --help: Usage: urx [OPTIONS] [DOMAINS]... [COMMAND] Commands: cache Inspect and maintain the URL cache (stats, list, prune, drop, clear) help Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s) Arguments: [DOMAINS]... Domains to fetch URLs for Options: -c, --config <CONFIG> Config file to load --provider-config <PATH> Separate provider config holding only API keys (default: ~/.config/urx/provider-config.toml; %APPDATA%\urx\provider-config.toml on Windows) --completions <SHELL> Print a shell completion script (bash, zsh, fish, powershell, elvish) to stdout and exit --manpage Print the roff man page to stdout and exit -h, --help Print help -V, --version Print version Input Options: --files <FILES>... Read URLs directly from files (supports WARC, URLTeam compressed, and text files) --domain-list <PATH> File of newline-separated domains to scan (repeatable; merged with positional DOMAINS; stdin is read only when they name no domains; `#` comments allowed) [alias: --dL] Output Options: -o, --output <OUTPUT> Output file to write results --output-dir <PATH> Write one file per URL host into this directory; extension matches --format. Coexists with --output / stdout. [alias: --oD] -f, --format <FORMAT> Output format: "plain", "json", "jsonl", "csv", "wordlist" (case-insensitive; anything else is a usage error) [default: plain] --merge-endpoint Merge endpoints with the same path and merge URL parameters --stream Write URLs as providers report them (plain/jsonl/csv only; unsorted; bypasses cache) --normalize-url Normalize URLs for better deduplication --dedup-similar Collapse URLs differing only in ids, hashes, dates, or query values --params Replace the URL list with every query parameter name the run saw, once each --params-by-endpoint One line per endpoint: the endpoint and the union of the parameter names seen on it --fuzz-placeholder <VALUE> Replace every query parameter value with VALUE, one URL per parameter signature Provider Options: --providers <PROVIDERS> Providers to use (comma-separated) [default: wayback,cc,otx] --exclude-providers <PROVIDERS> Providers to exclude (wins on conflict) --all-providers Enable every supported provider (API-keyed ones only if a key is available) --list-providers List every supported provider then exit --subs Include subdomains when searching --cc-index <CC_INDEX> Common Crawl index(es), comma-separated for parallel queries; `latest` auto-resolves [default: latest] --cdx-endpoint <URL> Query an additional CDX index server (pywb / OutbackCDX / classic) by its API URL; repeatable; id `cdx:<host>` (`cdx:<host>:<port>` with a port) --cdx-dialect <DIALECT> Dialect of the --cdx-endpoint servers: `pywb` or `classic` (unset: probed once, pywb fallback) --from <DATE> Restrict CDX providers to captures >= DATE (YYYY/YYYYMM/YYYYMMDD/YYYYMMDDhhmmss); legacy alias --wayback-from --to <DATE> Restrict CDX providers to captures <= DATE (same format as --from); legacy alias --wayback-to --archive-status <CODE> Keep only captures the archive recorded with this status code (a list works on wayback/classic endpoints only) --archive-exclude-status <CODES> Drop captures the archive recorded with these status codes --archive-mime <TYPE> Keep only captures with this recorded MIME type (a list works on wayback/classic endpoints only) --archive-exclude-mime <TYPES> Drop captures with these recorded MIME types --vt-api-key <VT_API_KEY> API key for VirusTotal --urlscan-api-key <URLSCAN_API_KEY> Optional API key for Urlscan (also works anonymously) --zoomeye-api-key <ZOOMEYE_API_KEY> API key for ZoomEye --github-api-key <GITHUB_API_KEY> Personal access token for GitHub Code Search (URX_GITHUB_API_KEY) --bevigil-api-key <BEVIGIL_API_KEY> API key for BeVigil, URLs from unpacked Android apps (URX_BEVIGIL_API_KEY) Discovery Options: --exclude-robots Exclude robots.txt discovery --exclude-sitemap Exclude sitemap.xml discovery --archived-discovery Also read every distinct archived version of robots.txt and sitemap.xml (see "Archived robots.txt and sitemap.xml" below) --archived-discovery-limit <N> Maximum archived documents fetched per domain by each archived provider; nested sitemaps count [default: 50] Display Options: -v, --verbose Show verbose output --silent Silent mode (no output) --no-progress No progress bar --no-color Disable ANSI color (NO_COLOR is also honored) --show-sources Annotate output URLs with the providers that returned them --show-meta Annotate plain-text URLs with the archive capture metadata --stats Print a per-provider summary to stderr at end of run Filter Options: -p, --preset <PRESET> Filter Presets (e.g., "no-resources,no-images,only-js,only-secrets,only-api") -e, --extensions <EXTENSIONS> Filter by extensions (e.g., "js,php,aspx") --exclude-extensions <EXTENSIONS> Exclude extensions (e.g., "html,txt") --patterns <PATTERNS> Include URLs containing patterns --exclude-patterns <PATTERNS> Exclude URLs containing patterns --match-regex <RE> Keep only URLs matching this regex (repeatable, ORed, case-sensitive) --filter-regex <RE> Drop URLs matching this regex (repeatable; one match is enough) --show-only-host Only show the host part --show-only-path Only show the path part --show-only-param Only show the parameters part --min-length <MIN_LENGTH> Minimum URL length --max-length <MAX_LENGTH> Maximum URL length --strict Enforce exact host validation (default) --no-strict Disable host validation; a target's path scope still applies (wins over --strict) --scope-file <FILE> Bug-bounty host scope file (`!` excludes, `*.host` wildcard, `[2001:db8::1]` exact IPv6); repeatable --meta-first-seen-after <DATE> Keep URLs whose oldest archived capture is on or after DATE --meta-first-seen-before <DATE> Keep URLs whose oldest archived capture is on or before DATE --meta-last-seen-after <DATE> Keep URLs whose newest archived capture is on or after DATE ("still alive as of") --meta-last-seen-before <DATE> Keep URLs whose newest archived capture is on or before DATE ("dead since") --meta-mime <TYPE> Keep only URLs with these archived MIME types (`image/*` matches any subtype) --meta-exclude-mime <TYPE> Drop URLs with these archived MIME types --meta-status <CODE> Keep only URLs with these archived status codes (20x / 5xx patterns) --meta-exclude-status <CODE> Drop URLs with these archived status codes Network Options: --network-scope <SCOPE> Apply settings to: all, providers, testers, providers,testers [default: all] --proxy <PROXY> HTTP proxy (e.g., http://proxy:8080) --proxy-auth <PROXY_AUTH> Proxy credentials (username:password) --insecure Skip SSL certificate verification --random-agent Use a random User-Agent -H, --header <NAME: VALUE> Extra request header, repeatable; sent to the target only, never to an archive --cookie <COOKIES> Cookie header for requests to the target --user-agent <STRING> User-Agent for requests to the target, overriding --random-agent --timeout <TIMEOUT> Request timeout in seconds [default: 120] --retries <RETRIES> Retries for failed requests [default: 2] --parallel <PARALLEL> Max domains fetched concurrently per provider, and concurrent URL tests (rate-limit shared) [default: 5] --rate-limit <RATE_LIMIT> Requests per second --rate-limit-by <PAIRS> Per-provider rate overrides (e.g. `vt=1,wayback=10`); falls back to --rate-limit for unlisted providers --max-time <SECONDS> Global ceiling on provider enumeration time in seconds; in-flight fetches are aborted at deadline (0 = unlimited) [default: 0] Testing Options: --check-status Check HTTP status code of collected URLs [alias: --cs] --include-status <INCLUDE_STATUS> Include specific status codes (e.g., 200,30x); implies the status check [alias: --is] --exclude-status <EXCLUDE_STATUS> Exclude specific status codes (e.g., 404,50x); implies the status check [alias: --es] --extract-links Extract additional links from collected URLs (see "Link Extraction" below) --extract-js-endpoints Fetch collected JavaScript and extract the endpoints in its string literals; with --archive-body also mines archived scripts (see "JavaScript Endpoint Extraction" below) --max-js-files <N> Maximum number of files --extract-js-endpoints will fetch (0 = unlimited) [default: 500] --archive-body Extract links from the *archived* body of each collected URL (see "Archived Response Bodies" below) --archive-body-limit <N> Maximum archived bodies fetched per run; bounds distinct bodies, not URLs [default: 500] --archive-body-dir <DIR> Keep every replayed body in DIR with an index.jsonl mapping it back to its URL --expand-specs Fetch collected OpenAPI/Swagger/GraphQL documents and expand every route they describe (see "API Specification Expansion" below) --max-spec-files <N> Maximum number of specification documents --expand-specs will fetch (0 = unlimited) [default: 50] --check-title Also record each response's HTML <title>; implies --check-status Cache Options: --incremental Only return new URLs compared to previous scans --cache-type <CACHE_TYPE> Cache backend: sqlite or redis [default: sqlite] --cache-path <CACHE_PATH> Path for SQLite cache database --redis-url <REDIS_URL> Redis connection URL --cache-ttl <CACHE_TTL> Cache TTL in seconds [default: 86400] --no-cache Disable caching entirely Notification Options: --notify <URL> POST a run summary to this webhook when the run ends (repeatable; also URX_NOTIFY_URL, provider-config `notify_url`, or `[notify].url`) --notify-on <NOTIFY_ON> When to send: new (only if URLs were emitted), always, or never [default: new] --notify-format <NOTIFY_FORMAT> Payload shape: json (urx summary), slack ({"text"}), or discord ({"content"}) [default: json] urx cache is the only subcommand. See Inspecting and Maintaining the Cache. Everything else on this page applies to a scan. Webhook Notifications --notify <URL> POSTs a run summary to a webhook when the run ends. Run it from cron with --incremental and it fires only when the archives have something new. # slack, only when new URLs turned up (default --notify-on new) urx target.com --incremental --silent \ --notify https://hooks.slack.com/services/T000/B000/XXXX --notify-format slack # discord, every run urx target.com --incremental --notify "$DISCORD_HOOK" --notify-format discord --notify-on always # several receivers, urx JSON schema urx target.com --incremental --notify https://n8n.example/hook --notify https://ntfy.example/urx # keep the webhook out of shell history export URX_NOTIFY_URL=https://hooks.slack.com/services/... urx target.com --incremental --notify-format slack --silent still sends, but it also hides the URL list on stdout. Add -o to keep the results. When it sends --notify-on Sends new (default) Only when the run emitted at least one URL. Under --incremental, at least one URL the previous run had not seen. always After every run, including one with zero URLs. never Nothing. The configuration stays in place. Payload formats json (default) uses urx's own schema: { "tool": "urx", "version": "0.11.0", "domains": ["example.com"], "incremental": true, "url_count": 12, "new_url_count": 12, "elapsed_ms": 3210, "providers": [ {"name": "Wayback Machine", "urls": 1200, "errors": 0, "partial": 0, "elapsed_ms": 2500, "aborted": false} ], "sample": ["https://example.com/api/v2/users", "..."], "sample_truncated": false } incremental is true only when the run diffed against the cache, so it is false under --no-cache or --files. providers has the same numbers --stats prints. sample holds up to 20 emitted URLs in output order, and sample_truncated is true when there were more. Under --stream the payload has the count and an empty sample (sample_truncated is true if any URL was emitted). slack sends {"text": "..."} and discord sends {"content": "..."}. The message is a header line (count, targets, elapsed time), one line of provider totals, the URL sample, and … N more not shown when the sample is short of the total. The text is cut on a line boundary at 2000 characters for Discord and 4000 for Slack, and ends with [truncated: N lines cut to fit the message limit]. A URL is never split. Archived URLs cannot ping anyone: Slack text escapes &, < and >, and the Discord payload sets "allowed_mentions": {"parse": []}. Failure handling Delivery never changes the exit code. The URLs are already on stdout or in --output, so a webhook that is down, slow or returns 4xx/5xx prints a warning on stderr and the run exits 0. --verbose prints the HTTP status of each delivery; --silent hides those lines but still sends. Each URL is tried once with no retry: chat webhooks are not idempotent, and a retry after a slow but delivered request would post twice. The URL is a secret A Slack or Discord webhook URL is the credential. urx prints only its scheme, host and non-default port (https://hooks.slack.com) in verbose output, warnings, --stats and error text, and the payload never contains it. To keep it out of a checked-in config, use the URX_NOTIFY_URL environment variable or notify_url in the provider-config file. [notify].url in the main config also works. Precedence is CLI/env > provider-config > main config, the same as API keys. The [notify] section also takes on and format (the config equivalents of --notify-on and --notify-format). Network settings The request uses --proxy, --proxy-auth, --timeout and --insecure. --network-scope does not apply: it splits traffic between the archives (providers) and the target (testers), and the webhook is your own endpoint. Archive Capture Metadata The CDX-backed providers (wayback, cc, arquivo, and any --cdx-endpoint) return captures, so each URL comes with these fields: Field Meaning first_seen Oldest capture timestamp, 14-digit CDX form (YYYYMMDDhhmmss) last_seen Newest capture timestamp mime MIME type of the most recent capture that recorded one archive_status HTTP status the archive recorded at capture time digest A representative content digest across the captures archive_status is what the crawler got at capture time. status (only under --check-status) comes from requesting the URL live now. A URL can have archive_status 200 and be dead today. When the same URL comes from several captures or archives, the fields merge: first_seen is the oldest timestamp, last_seen the newest, and mime/archive_status come from the most recent capture that had them. Wayback returns one capture per URL, its newest, so from Wayback alone first_seen equals last_seen. Providers with no capture index (otx, vt, urlscan, zoomeye, github, bevigil, robots, sitemap) and --files input report the URL only. A domain served from cache has no metadata either (the cache stores URLs only); use --no-cache to get it back. Format Output json / jsonl A key per field, only when it has a value csv A column per field, only when at least one row has a value plain Bare URL by default. --show-meta appends [first_seen=… last_seen=… mime=…] A URL rewritten by --normalize-url or --merge-endpoint no longer matches what the providers reported, so it has no sources or capture metadata. URLs served from cache, or found by --extract-links, --extract-js-endpoints, --archive-body or --expand-specs, have no sources. --show-sources and --show-meta are rejected under --stream. A streamed URL is printed on first sighting, before other providers or later captures could add to it. urx example.com --providers wayback -f jsonl # {"url":"https://example.com/old.php","first_seen":"20040112093000", # "last_seen":"20180722140311","mime":"text/html","archive_status":"200", # "digest":"HT2DYGA5UKZCPBSFVCV3JOBXGW2G5UUA"} # everything last captured before 2010 urx example.com -f jsonl | jq -r 'select(.last_seen and .last_seen < "20100101000000") | .url' # metadata in plain output urx example.com --providers wayback --show-meta Live Response Metadata --check-status records these fields from the response head along with the status: Field Meaning status Code and reason (200 OK), or Status check failed when the request failed (connection refused, timeout, TLS). It reads at most 64 KiB (checked between chunks), stops at the closing tag, and skips bodies the server declared as non-HTML. The title is whitespace-collapsed, entity-decoded and cut to 200 characters (with a trailing … when longer). Use it with --providers, --exclude-providers and --rate-limit-by; --stats and --show-sources show it. Naming an endpoint enables it. It honours --subs, --from/--to, the --archive-* filters, pagination and rate limiting like wayback/cc/arquivo, and reports capture metadata. --cdx-dialect classic|pywb sets the server's dialect (field names, filter semantics, row format, pagination; see Archive-side Filtering). Unset, urx probes once per run and falls back to pywb. Set it when the probe can't tell, e.g. the server gives an empty answer for an unknown domain. Config file: cdx_endpoint = [...] and cdx_dialect under [provider]. The only public endpoint verified to work is https://vefsafn.is/cdx (Iceland, pywb). It ignores limit, page and showNumPages and returns the whole result set, which urx handles. After a few requests it may answer with an Anubis-style "Session Verification" page. urx reports that as an error naming the endpoint, never as an empty result. Slow down with --rate-limit-by cdx:vefsafn.is=1 or retry later. Positional domains and --domain-list are ignored. --files takes several paths, so a domain placed after it is read as another file. No host validation, since there is no target. Use --scope-file or --match-regex to restrict hosts. Every URL is attributed to file in --show-sources and --stats. Filters, testers and output options work as usual. --stream is rejected; the cache and --incremental are not used. The format is picked by file name: File name Read as .warc WARC .gz or .bz2 WARC if the name contains warc, otherwise URLTeam .txt or .list text other, containing warc WARC other, containing urlteam / url_team URLTeam anything else text WARC and URLTeam files are checked for gzip by magic bytes, and multi-member streams are read in full. Text files are never decompressed: a gzip or bzip2 file with a text name yields no URLs and no error, so give it a .gz extension or decompress it first. The WARC and URLTeam readers do not support bzip2: the run stops with bzip2 input is not supported. Decompress it first (bzip2 WARC input… for a WARC) and exits 1. Lines over 1 MiB are skipped. Hitting a cap prints a warning. urx --files urls.txt --check-status --include-status 200 urx --files crawl.warc.gz --scope-file scope.txt -f jsonl Shell Completions and the Man Page Both are generated by the binary, so they match the installed version. Substring shape rules are checked against the lower-cased path, query and fragment (never the host). So only-secrets catches /.env (no extension) and only-backup catches /index.php~.
